title: Boy spots mouse deer trapped in deep drain on way to school, asks father to help
text:
Boy spots mouse deer trapped in deep drain on way to school, asks father to help | Lianhe Zaobao 
 Singapore International China Business Opinion Lifestyle Entertainment Search Matthew Yau Published / 16 Nov 2026 17:30 S M L XL Boy spots mouse deer trapped in deep drain on way to school, asks father to help
 AI-translated article with transliterated names. Read original Chinese article here. 
 Unable to climb out, the mouse deer sat quietly in the drain, which was about five metres deep. （Courtesy of interviewee） A seven-year-old boy on his way to school spotted a “little deer” trapped in a deep drain and immediately asked his father to help rescue it. His father called the National Parks Board (NParks), whose officers arrived swiftly and rescued the frightened animal. It was no ordinary deer, but a mouse deer. 
 Graphic designer Ashz Loy, 55, shared the encounter in a Facebook post last Thursday (12 November). He said he was taking his son Ethan to school that morning when the boy spotted a “little deer” trapped in a large drain, unable to climb out. Ethan, who loves animals, immediately asked his father to find a way to save the poor creature. 
 The drain was too deep for Loy to climb into. After dropping his son off at school, he called NParks for help. The agency responded swiftly, sending officers to the scene soon afterwards. 
 Videos and photographs uploaded by Ashz Loy showed that the trapped animal was a mouse deer, sitting quietly in a drain about five metres deep. Two National Parks Board (NParks) officers worked together: one stayed at street level to monitor the situation while the other climbed down into the drain with a net and slowly approached the mouse deer. 
 As the officer approached, the mouse deer suddenly charged towards him. He immediately swung his net to intercept it, but the nimble animal turned in an instant and darted in the opposite direction. The experienced officer quickly changed direction and deftly caught the mouse deer in his net, bringing it to safety. 
 In his post, Loy paid tribute to the NParks officers and said his son would be delighted to see the photographs and videos when he returned home from school. 
 Boy mistakes mouse deer for capybara on first encounter 
 Lianhe Zaobao contacted Loy on Monday (16). He said his son had spotted the trapped mouse deer at 7am on the day of the incident, in a drain in front of HDB Block 404 Fajar Road in Bukit Panjang. 
 Loy said his son initially thought it was a capybara. “It was our first time seeing a mouse deer. We also noticed two crows nearby attacking it.” 
 Father and son were very worried about the mouse deer, but fortunately there were no monitor lizards nearby. “Monitor lizards are usually found in this drain after it rains. I’m glad the NParks officers arrived in time and rescued the mouse deer safely.” 
 With a laugh, Loy said his son was delighted to see the rescue photographs and immediately asked if he could take him to the zoo to visit the mouse deer. “He really loves animals.” 
 NParks captures mouse deer, releases it the same day after assessment 
 Responding to queries from Lianhe Zaobao, How Choon Beng, senior director of wildlife management at the National Parks Board (NParks), confirmed that officers had successfully captured the mouse deer that morning and taken it to Mandai Wildlife Centre for assessment. 
 How said the mouse deer was released at Chestnut Nature Park the same day after an examination confirmed it was healthy and fit to return to the wild. 
 NParks reminded the public not to approach or handle wildlife themselves. Anyone who spots a wild animal in need of urgent rescue can call its 24-hour Animal Response Centre hotline on 1800-476-1600. 
 In another recent animal rescue in Singapore, a chicken was saved after falling into a drain. A video posted online last week showed a shirtless man wading into the drain to help the chicken, which had fallen in for unknown reasons. He scooped it up with a plastic bag, then climbed over a wall to get out. The amusing “heroic chicken rescue” drew praise from many netizens.
